dict.string:
Brightwheel — Attendance
Checks your children in or out by talking to the Brightwheel API directly, without opening the app. Who the children are, which room they are in and who is checking them in all come from Brightwheel when it runs — nothing about your family is built into this shortcut.
Brightwheel Check In and Brightwheel Check Out start this one and tell it which direction to go; those are the two that carry the automation triggers. Run this on its own and it simply asks.
Built to be run unattended by a location trigger, so it does not stop to ask anything on the normal path. Everything it needs is collected once, when you import it. When it should run is decided by the trigger's own time range, not by this shortcut.
Each run: 1. Checks the saved sign-in is still valid, and signs in again by itself if it has expired. 2. Looks up whether each child is already checked in or out. 3. Skips anyone already the way this run wants them, so running it twice is harmless. 4. Sends the request for everyone else and posts a notification per child.

This shortcut saves the Brightwheel session token in its own on-device storage and refreshes it automatically, because a background automation cannot stop to ask you to paste a new one.
The three values below are filled in when you import the shortcut, so neither your password nor your check-in code is stored in the shortcut file itself. Your session token is never in the file either: it is kept under this shortcut, so deleting the shortcut takes the token with it.
The school's code is the one thing kept outside this shortcut, so that re-importing does not send you back for the QR code. "Forget saved sign-in and school code" in the menu clears both.
If you ever share or export this shortcut, clear the three Text actions below first. The check-in code authenticates as you.
Work out which direction this run goes. - Condition counts whether a direction was handed in - Brightwheel Check In and Check Out hand one in - Run on its own there is none, so it asks instead
Ask, when nothing was handed in. - Each choice sets Direction to the same in or out a wrapper would - Canceling the menu stops the shortcut, so nothing is sent

array.string: Forget saved sign-in and school code

dict.string: Check the children in or out?

Draw the stored code, or say there is none. - Condition counts whether anything is stored, because an empty string still satisfies "has any value" - Condition 2 against 0 is "more than none", so the first branch is the one where a code exists - Nothing is stored until the first run at the school has scanned it
Run a check-in at the school once. It scans the code by the door and keeps it.
Forget saved sign-in and school code
The next run signs in again and asks you to scan the school's code.

Set the wording and the value Brightwheel expects. - The key is the direction, so in and out read the same three fields - Checked In Value goes into the request as true or false - Verb and Already Word are only used in notifications
--- SETUP --- These three values are requested when the shortcut is imported. To change one later, edit the matching Text action, or re-import the shortcut.

--- SESSION --- Use the token saved by the last sign-in. There is none the first time, so the first run signs in and saves one.
The token is kept under this shortcut rather than in the shared store, so deleting the shortcut clears it and a re-import signs in again. The school's code is kept in the shared store instead, and outlives both.

Sign in again, up to five times. - Each pass asks Brightwheel to send a fresh code, then asks you for it - Leaving the box empty, or typing resend, sends another code instead of trying to use what was typed - Canceling the code prompt stops the whole shortcut - A pass that gets a token clears Needs Sign In, so later passes do nothing
Only act while the session is still not usable. - Condition checks whether an earlier pass already signed in
Enter the 6-digit code Brightwheel emailed. No code yet? Leave this empty, or type resend, and another will be sent. Cancel stops the shortcut.
Only try the code if one was actually entered. - Condition counts whether the answer is six digits - Anything else falls through, and the next pass sends a new code
Keep the new token when the code was accepted. - Condition counts whether a token came back - A wrong or expired code returns none, and the next pass asks again
Give up after five attempts. - Condition checks whether the session is still unusable - Nothing has been sent to Brightwheel about the children yet
Could not sign in after five tries, so nothing was sent. Run this shortcut by hand and enter a code, or leave the box empty to have another sent.
Fetch the guardian id if signing in meant the first read missed it. - Condition counts whether an id was found on the probe - The probe body is the auth error on a run that had to sign in
Stop if the account could not be identified. - Condition counts whether a guardian id was read - An empty one would 404 the roster call and read as an empty roster
Could not read which Brightwheel account this is, so nothing was sent. Run this shortcut by hand to try again.

--- WHO TO SEND FOR --- Nobody is named in here. The children come from Brightwheel itself, a little further down, which is why adding or moving one needs no rebuild. What this sets is the flag that lets the whole send run a second time if the school's code turns out to be stale.

Send, and send again once if the school code turned out to be stale. - Send Needed starts at yes, and is set again only by a rejected code - A child already in the right state is skipped, so a second pass cannot double up on anyone who already succeeded
Do nothing on the second pass unless one was asked for. - Condition checks whether a send is still outstanding - Only a rejected school code asks for another pass

Scan the school's code when there is none saved. - Condition counts whether anything is stored - Nothing is stored on the first run, or after a stale code was forgotten below - Show Alert explains what to point the camera at before it opens
The school's check-in QR code is needed. Point the camera at the code on the sign-in tablet.
Warn if the school has started requiring signatures. - Condition counts whether the scanned code says signatures are on - Check-ins send no signature, so they would start failing
These shortcuts do not send one, so check-ins may start failing.
Ask Brightwheel who the children are and where they stand. - One call returns the roster and each child's current state - Nothing about the family is built into this shortcut
Rescan if the school's code was rotated. - Condition counts whether the roster call rejected the code - Forgetting it makes the second pass scan a fresh one
Scanning the new one and trying again.
The school's check-in code has changed
Did Brightwheel list any children? - Condition counts the children in the reply - An error reply has none, and would read as nobody to send for
Brightwheel did not return a roster, so nothing was sent. Open the app to check, and run this by hand.
Does every room entry carry a state? - Condition counts children minus check-in states - A room that has lost the key reads as nobody to send for
A room in the roster has no check-in state, so nothing was sent rather than sending for only some of them.
Look at each child's own rooms in turn. - One pass that sends nothing, so a bad child stops the whole run - Both checks below fire per child, so two bad children say so twice
Does this child have a room at all? - Condition counts this child's own room entries - None means there is no room to send them to
A child in the roster has no room, so nothing was sent rather than sending for only some of them.
Is this child in more than one room? - Condition counts this child's own room entries - The room to send would be a guess, so nobody is
A child is listed in more than one room, so nothing was sent rather than guessing which one to use.
Only send if every check above agreed. - Condition counts whether the roster survived all of them - Anything else has already said why, and sends nothing

Work through the children in turn. - Each child arrives whole, so their name, id and room are read straight off them rather than looked up - Their current state is the checked_in flag on the room they are in, which came back with the roster and so cannot disagree with it

Skip anyone who needs no change. - Condition counts whether their state and this run disagree - This is also what makes a second pass safe after a rescan - If the state cannot be read, the request is sent anyway
Report the result. - Condition counts whether Brightwheel really recorded something - Otherwise branch works out whether the school code was the problem

Tell a stale school code apart from anything else. - Condition counts whether Brightwheel rejected the school's code - Forgetting it makes this run scan a fresh one and try again - Otherwise branch just reports what Brightwheel said
Scanning the new one and trying again.
The school's check-in code has changed

￼
If this says the session expired, run this shortcut by hand to sign in again.
Brightwheel account email — Used to sign in again when the session token stops working.

Brightwheel account password — Used together with the email, only when signing in again.
Passwords are case-sensitive, and this field capitalizes the first letter for you. Check it matches your password exactly before moving on.

Brightwheel check-in code — Your 4-digit guardian check-in code.
iOS 27: if “Add Shortcut” does nothing when you tap it, tap “Skip Setup” instead — it saves these answers too. That is an iOS bug, not a problem with what you typed.
